description:
## Why

PKIX-xj81 decomposition, pattern 4 of 6. Pool admits two same-length valid
paths from EE to anchor. Document the deterministic tiebreak contract and
test it.

## What

Pool topology:

```
StressRoot ── signs ── IntermediateA ── signs ── PathChoiceEE
StressRoot ── signs ── IntermediateB ── signs ── PathChoiceEE
```

(Same EE, dual issuers — only possible if EE is signed by two issuers, i.e.
two separate EE certs with the same DN + SPKI, each signed by a different
intermediate. So the fixture actually has PathChoiceEE-A and PathChoiceEE-B
that share subject DN + SPKI; the build is from any one of them.)

Actual fixture:

```
StressRoot ── signs ── IntermediateA (SKI=keyA)
StressRoot ── signs ── IntermediateB (SKI=keyB)
IntermediateA ── signs ── PathChoiceEE_A (AKI=keyA, same SPKI as B)
IntermediateB ── signs ── PathChoiceEE_B (AKI=keyB, same SPKI as A)
```

(Two EE certs with the same subject DN and SPKI but signed by different
intermediates; AKI distinguishes them. PKIX-yn3e behaviour means the AKI
hint determines which intermediate is tried first.)

Build steps:

1. Generator issues five DER fixtures.
2. Test (`tests/path_disambiguation.rs`):
   - For PathChoiceEE_A with AKI=keyA: `build_path` must return a chain
     containing IntermediateA, not IntermediateB. Verify via SKI bytes.
   - For PathChoiceEE_B with AKI=keyB: `build_path` must return IntermediateB.
   - When AKI is absent (third EE variant, but no AKI), document the
     observed tiebreak (pool-insertion order today) in the test as a
     pinned contract.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Five+ DER fixtures committed.
- [ ] Generation reproducible via `generate.sh`.
- [ ] Three integration tests pinning the tiebreak behaviour.

## Depends on

PKIX-xj81.1.
